output.reason: A 6-month-old with reported fever, fussiness, reduced feeding interest and fewer wet diapers today needs hands-on hydration and perfusion assessment plus possible urine testing today, which messaging cannot provide.
output.patientMessage: Please have your baby seen in person today — urgent pediatric or urgent care. Fever with poor feeding and fewer wet diapers in a 6-month-old needs a hands-on check of hydration and a possible urine test. Go to the emergency department right away instead if she becomes hard to wake, limp, breathes fast or hard, has a stiff neck, a spreading rash, or stops drinking altogether.
differential: Febrile infection with dehydration from poor intake

output.evidenceLimitations: Sources are emergency-department synthesis references for pediatric fever, not telehealth triage protocols, and much of the detail concerns neonates rather than a 6-month-old.

citations.claim: Poor feeding is listed among features marking a febrile infant as higher-risk/ill-appearing, supporting in-person appearance assessment.
citations.limitation: Appearance grading requires hands-on exam; other listed features are unreported here.
